function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.content:
I’m afraid I don’t have a built‑in “reverse‑geocode” helper in this sandbox – the only HTTP wrapper we’ve got here (`requests_get`) talks to the **Open Meteo** weather API, so it won’t give us an address back.

That said, getting an address from those coordinates is straightforward if you hit a real geocoding service yourself. Below are two common options:

| Service | Endpoint Example | Notes |
|---------|------------------|-------|
| **Google Maps Geocoding API** | `https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/geocode/json?latlng=37.4224764,-122.0842499&key=<YOUR_API_KEY>` | Requires a billing account & API key. Returns full formatted address plus components. |
| **Nominatim (OSM)** | `https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/reverse?format=jsonv2&lat=37.4224764&lon=-122.0842499` | Free tier, polite usage required (max 1 req/s), includes display_name. |

### Quick test with cURL / curl

```bash
curl "https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/reverse?format=jsonv2&lat=37.4224764&lon=-122.0842499"
```

Typical JSON snippet returned:

```json
{
  "place_id": "...",
  "licence": "...",
  "osm_type": "node",
  "osm_id": "...",
  "lat": "37.4224764",
  "lon": "-122.0842499",
  "display_name": "1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, Santa Clara County, California, 94043, United States",
  ...
}
```

If you prefer the Google version, just replace `<YOUR_API_KEY>` with your actual key:

```bash
curl "https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/geocode/json?latlng=37.4224764,-122.0842499&key=AIzaSyD..."
```

And parse out `"formatted_address"` from the resulting JSON.

---

#### What you could do programmatically (Python)

```python
import requests

def reverse_geocode(lat, lon):
    url = f"https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/reverse"
    params = {
        "format": "jsonv2",
        "lat": lat,
        "lon": lon,
    }
    headers = {"User-Agent": "MyApp/1.0"}   # Nominatim requires a unique User-Agent
    resp = requests.get(url, params=params, headers=headers)
    return resp.json()["display_name"]

print(reverse_geocode(37.4224764, -122.0842499))
```

This will print something along the lines of:

> *“1600 Amphitheatre Pkwy, Mountain View, CA 94043, USA”*

Feel free to swap in the Google endpoint if you already have a key—just adjust the parameter names (`latlng=` instead of separate `lat/lon`). Let me know if you'd like more details on handling rate limits, caching results, or integrating into a larger app!
